messages:
maria: Heads-up — ran the nightly kernel selector sweep on a mixed-head-size workload (headdim 30/48/64) and we're seeing non-causal SDPA v2 picked for some causal requests when headdim==30. latency up ~1.9x for those slices.

arjun: that sounds bad. can you paste the selector decision trace?

maria: pasted below. this is from the selector logs on sm80 box: 

```
[selector] model=xl-8b, seq=128, headdim=30, causal=true, gpu=sm80
candidates: [sdpa_v1_noncausal, sdpa_v2_causal, flashv3_causal]
score(sdpa_v1_noncausal)=0.22, score(sdpa_v2_causal)=0.19, score(flashv3_causal)=0.17
chosen=sdpa_v1_noncausal (fallback_policy: prefer_lower_mem)
```

maria: note: sdpa_v1_noncausal lacks causal-optimized tiling so it triggers a slower path and disables some KV cache streamlining.

liam: hmm selector picked non-causal even though a causal variant had slightly better runtime score? scores look lower => better, but chosen is the first candidate with policy tie?

arjun: the comment shows scores where v2_causal=0.19 and v1_noncausal=0.22 (higher). shouldn't we pick lower score? maybe a bug inverted comparison during architecture aware tie-breaking.

maria: yep I double-checked — the runtime had an if-statement that compared "<" vs ">" for sm80 branches during the arch-aware ranking. patch incoming. but also want to discuss whether our fallback policy "prefer_lower_mem" is causing non-causal picks for headdim 30 specifically.

liam: why is headdim 30 special? I thought thresholds were around 32/48 boundaries.

maria: it's the model tokenizer pad/packing we use — some microbatches create kv cache shape that produces headdim remap to 30 (3x10) on older quantized kernels. flash/SDPA kernels have heuristics that expect even multiples; v2's tiling thrives on 32-based head sizes, v1 has generic slower path that tolerates odd sizes.

liam: got it. two action items then: 1) fix comparator bug, 2) adjust fallback pick order so causal variants are preferred for causal requests even if mem score slightly worse.

arjun: also add a small penalty in the selector for kernels that disable KV streaming (we saw 18% extra token-cost). put it behind a guard flag so we can ramp.

maria: I ran a quick perf diff after forcing v2_causal for those traces — results: 

```
perf summary (headdim=30, seq=128, bs=1):
- sdpa_v1_noncausal: p50=62ms, p95=95ms
- sdpa_v2_causal (forced): p50=33ms, p95=51ms
- flashv3_causal: p50=28ms, p95=45ms
```

maria: so v2_causal is ~2x faster than the non-causal fallback. KV interactions explain the gap.

liam: nice repro. can you also dump KV cache allocation traces? I want to ensure no extra copies.

maria: attached snippet from trace (simplified): 
```
kv_alloc: backend=cualloc, size=3.6MB, flags=streaming_enabled=false
kv_copy: src=host->gpu (extra memcpy) at 0.003s
```

maria: forcing v2_causal enables streaming and removes memcpy.

arjun: dev-bot just reported a CI perf regression yesterday tied to sdpa selector changes — might be related. dev-bot, ping what job id?

dev-bot: [perf-monitor] Regression alert: job=perf-sweep-2026-03-15, trace=1765470000, metric=commit_latency_p50, delta=+28% for model xl-8b headdim=30 on sm80.

liam: ok that links. Maria — can you open a tiny PR for comparator fix + add selector test for headdim odd sizes? also add a canary config to enable KV-penalty param.

maria: will do. I'll also run a small sweep across sm86 & sm90 to confirm no arch-specific surprises.

arjun: thanks. if you want I can follow up to add an observability gauge that flags when "non-causal" kernels are chosen for causal routes — quick alert to avoid future regressions.

maria: please do that, arjun. adding a one-week alert should catch noisy rollouts. :thumbsup:
